market_mood: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia sparked a ~4.5% S&P melt-up that erased much of last week's AI-driven slump, while two quieter stories — a hawkish Fed comment from John Williams and a $44B CrowdStrike/Zscaler cybersecurity merger — got less attention.
self_check: My high-confidence calls have been much worse than my low-confidence ones (7% vs 51%), and bullish chases of already-moving news have been my biggest losers, so today I avoided the Nvidia bounce entirely and used no high confidence.

picks.reason: Reuters flags a stubborn global diesel shortage even as crude has calmed, which keeps refining margins fat; energy was the weakest sector last week so this is not crowded.
Fed's John Williams said rates likely need to go higher over time to finish the inflation job, which argues against long-dated bonds while the market is distracted by the Nvidia story.
Target has out-comped Walmart three quarters in a row with 5.6% comps yet trades at less than half Walmart's multiple, and retail earnings showed consumer spending holding up outside apparel.
ESPN and the NFL expand Super Bowl 61 distribution to Imax, Disney+ and ABC.
Higher-for-longer rate talk plus depressed home turnover is a bad mix for housing.

watchlist_notes.note: Jumped ~4.7% on the Huang news, so the easy relief bounce is done; Williams' hawkish rate talk is the offset.
Tech led the rally (IT sector +8.6%), leaving the index vulnerable if the AI enthusiasm fades again.
Rose with the broad market but lags the AI-heavy indexes; rate comments matter more here.
Rallied with the tech tape but had no company-specific news today.
Lifted by the AI rebound; server cost inflation from Dell/HPE price hikes is a modest headwind to capex budgets.
Up ~31% on Huang's reinstatement — the news is fully in the price, and China risk plus governance questions remain.
Bought Decart AI's chip-optimization tech, a small positive for its in-house silicon efficiency story.
Up ~6% in the AI rally with a fresh bullish Cramer call, but nothing new fundamentally.
No major news today beyond the broad AI-led rally.
Rose on tie-up chatter and a software rollout; headline-driven rather than fundamental.
Financials lagged the rally (+1.7%) and had a weak week; Williams' higher-rates view is a mild net positive for margins.
Energy was the worst sector last week, but tight diesel and Iran sanctions/blockade risk keep a floor under crude.
Firm commodity prices and a softer dollar support gold, but a hawkish Fed cuts the other way.
Williams signaling higher rates 'over time' and sticky core inflation are headwinds for long bonds.

top_buys.pitch: Diesel is tight even as crude calms down, and refiners get paid for that.
top_buys.why: Reuters says oil's recovery from the Iran conflict masks a stubborn diesel shortage, which is exactly what drives refining crack spreads. Energy was the worst-performing sector last week (-6%), so expectations are low and this isn't a crowded trade. Fresh US sanctions on Iran's shadow banking and blockade tensions add supply risk on top.
top_buys.risks: A quick de-escalation with Iran or a demand slowdown would compress margins fast, and refiners are volatile.
top_buys.watch: Weekly EIA distillate inventories and diesel crack spreads.

top_buys.pitch: Target is out-comping Walmart but trades at less than half the multiple.
top_buys.why: Coverage notes Target's comparable sales rose 5.6% and it has beaten Walmart's comps three quarters running, while Walmart trades at over 2x its multiple. Retail earnings last week showed consumer spending holding up outside apparel, which fits Target's broader mix. The valuation gap gives room to close if holiday traffic is decent.
top_buys.risks: Target has repeatedly disappointed on execution, and apparel weakness is a real part of its mix.
top_buys.watch: Black Friday and Cyber Monday traffic data and Target's holiday commentary.

top_buys.pitch: A top Fed official just said rates likely go higher over time, and bonds barely noticed.
top_buys.why: John Williams, one of the most influential FOMC voices, indicated higher rates are likely over time to finish the inflation job and only sees 2% near 2027. Commentary also notes core price pressures lingering with a still-strong economy. With the market fixated on Nvidia, this hawkish signal may take days to filter into long-end yields.
top_buys.risks: Any growth scare or equity reversal sends money straight back into long Treasuries.
top_buys.watch: Upcoming inflation prints and other Fed speakers echoing or softening Williams' message.

top_buys.pitch: ESPN and the NFL expand Super Bowl 61 distribution to Imax, Disney+ and ABC.
top_buys.why: Disney controls an unusually broad slate of distribution for the biggest US television event, which supports advertising pricing and Disney+ signups. The stock has been a market laggard with low expectations. These are incremental revenue streams the market isn't modeling.
top_buys.risks: One sporting event is small relative to Disney's whole business, and parks/linear trends matter far more.
top_buys.watch: Super Bowl ad pricing reports and Disney's next quarterly streaming subscriber numbers.

top_buys.pitch: Higher-for-longer rate talk plus depressed home turnover is a bad mix for housing.
top_buys.why: Williams signaled rates likely head higher over time, and Home Depot's outlook already flagged depressed home turnover. Homebuilder stocks rallied hard with the broad market today, which gives a better entry on the short side. Mortgage rates following Treasury yields up would hurt affordability further.
top_buys.risks: If the Fed turns dovish or yields fall, housing stocks bounce sharply.
top_buys.watch: 30-year mortgage rate trends and new home sales data.

summary.big_story: Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO triggered a ~4.5% S&P 500 surge, overshadowing a hawkish Fed signal and a $44B cybersecurity mega-merger.
summary.top_pick: Phillips 66, because a persistent diesel shortage keeps refining margins strong in the market's most beaten-down sector.
summary.watch: Whether the Nvidia-led bounce holds through the week and how bond yields react to Williams' 'higher rates over time' comment.
